query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Using a machine-learning-based potential (MLP) trained on ab initio molecular dynamics simulations can improve the representation of high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states near their melting temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states
generation.intervention: Machine-learning-based potential (MLP) training on ab initio molecular dynamics simulations
generation.conditions: Temperatures near the melting points of the alloys, composition ranges of 3-6 principal elements with concentrations between 10-40 at.%
generation.structural_mediator: Short-range order and medium-range order in the liquid and solid phases
generation.mechanism: Improved representation of atomic configurations through MLP, enhancing phase-space overlap between reference and target systems
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references, as measured by free-energy differences
generation.boundary: Composition ranges of 3-6 principal elements, temperature ranges within 100 K of the melting points
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the transferability of MLPs across different compositions and temperatures, potential limitations in the training data

falsification_experiment.design: Free-energy calculations using MLP and EAM references for a set of high-entropy alloys, comparison of the results to ab initio benchmarks
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the MLP-based free-energy differences deviate by more than 50 meV/atom from the ab initio benchmarks, the hypothesis is falsified
